text:
maria: Quick q — are our nightly DB backups and object-store snapshots encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys? Planning SOC2 update :thinking_face:
kevin: We encrypt RDS snapshots with KMS (CMK alias/redwood/backups). S3 bucket for backups uses SSE-KMS obj-level by default. Some old snapshots pre-2024 use SSE-S3, we should migrate those.
jon: Important: key policy + IAM must forbid broad iam:Decrypt. Use grants for services only, and conditions on kms:EncryptionContext when possible.
lisa_auditor: Confirming for docs: need proof of KMS rotation policy, key admin list, and CloudTrail logs for Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. Also retention window for audit logs.
maria: Good — two questions: 1) How do we handle EBS snapshots for dedicated instances (private) — are those encrypted with the same CMK? 2) Migration plan for old SSE-S3 objects?
kevin: EBS snapshots are encrypted at-create with the account CMK. For Dedicated/private we use a separate key per-tenant group alias/redwood/dedicated/<org>. Using separate CMKs simplifies RBAC and key revocation impact.
infra-sre: For existing unencrypted EBS snapshots the only safe path is create a copy with encryption (snap copy --encrypted) into an encrypted volume, then replace. That's I/O and time heavy but doable in maintenance windows.
jon: For S3 object migration we can run a serverless job: read object, call KMS GenerateDataKey with CMK, re-upload with SSE-KMS header. Alternatively, use S3 Batch Operations with a Lambda to re-encrypt objects — preserves metadata and is fast.
maria: Audit logging: where do we capture KMS API calls? We need them tied to incidents.
sec-bot: (automated) CloudTrail is logging KMS API events in prod. Trail: redwood-prod-audit, bucket: redwood-audit-logs, encryption: SSE-KMS alias/redwood/audit-logs. Alerts: CloudWatch metric filter for kms:Decrypt -> pager on anomaly.
jon: Ensure CloudTrail is set to READ_WRITE for all regions. Enable log file validation. Ship logs to central account and enable access only via secure role (assume-role limited time).
lisa_auditor: For SOC2: document the key rotation frequency, who can rotate, and a short runbook: steps to rotate CMK with minimal disruption (create new key, reencrypt data keys for in-flight tokens, update aliases, rotate backups).
kevin: Rotation note: enable automatic rotation for CMKs where supported, but for tenant CMKs we do manual rotation with alias swap after re-wrapping data keys. Test on a dev tenant first.
maria: Vulnerability triage: discovered a script that used SSE-S3 for an older backup lambda. Is this a sev2?
jon: Triage: If the script only wrote non-sensitive logs -> p3. If it wrote customer PII or DB dumps -> p1 and require immediate re-encryption + incident runbook.
kevin: Action items: 1) inventory all backup sources and class them (DB snapshots, EBS, S3 backups, snapshot exports). 2) Flag items using SSE-S3 or unencrypted. 3) Schedule re-encryption jobs and maintenance windows. 4) Update RBAC/key policies and document rotation.
maria: I'll create the inventory. Who volunteers to draft the runbook for key compromise?
jon: I can start the runbook. Include steps: revoke grants, disable key (not delete), update aliases, rekey backups from cold copies, notify legal/ops.
infra-sre: Add step: snapshot isolation for affected tenants and forensic copy to WORM bucket (write-once) with explicit retention.
lisa_auditor: Also add verification step: produce proof of re-encryption (log hashes + object metadata) for audit.
maria: Thanks — I'll open a follow-up ticket and link runbook. Quick ask: any gotchas for cross-account KMS usage with Dedicated customers?
kevin: Cross-account: use key policy to allow external account principal and prefer using KMS grants for short-lived access. Avoid broad wildcard principals. Make sure CMKs in central account have proper aliasing and per-tenant tags for billing.
jon: Also enforce iam:ViaService and kms:ViaService conditions where applicable to restrict usage to specific AWS services.
maria: Perfect. Wrapping up — schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to review inventory and runbook drafts. :calendar:
